extracted.intended_audience: prospective Penn State Law students, authors, and general readers interested in Penn State Law Review membership and publication
extracted.subtask_description: Describes Penn State Law Review's publication scope, membership selection process, associate-editor duties, editorial-board roles, and online companion content. Useful for students seeking membership or authors considering submission to the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal scope and topic eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Penn State Law Review is a general-interest journal that is run entirely by students, publishing a broad range of legal scholarship without limiting submissions to any specific topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal publishes legal articles written by scholars and professionals, and comments written by Penn State Law students; it does not restrict submissions to particular subject-matter areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection/publication standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles and comments meeting the standards of the editorial board are selected and published in the print edition of the Law Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page refers to a 'stringent selection process' evaluating submissions from outside scholars and student comments; specific editorial standards are determined by the editorial board (not enumerated on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership admissions criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Penn State Law Review extends annual membership invitations to rising second-year students at the conclusion of the spring semester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Of the available membership invitations, one-half are based upon grades and the other half are based upon evaluations of the write-on competition. The write-on competition commences during the summer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate editor source-checking and citation compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Associate editors are responsible for checking sources cited in the articles pending publication to ensure accuracy and compliance with the most recent edition of the Bluebook and Law Review local rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implies a standard of accurate sourcing and strict Bluebook/local-style conformity for all material proceeding to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate editor requirement to produce a publishable comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Associate editors are required to produce a legal comment of publishable quality on a topic of their choosing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once complete, the student-written comments are reviewed and graded by the Law Review comments editors, with the top scored comments selected for publication; thus quality is assessed via internal grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board composition and management responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Following successful completion of their duties as associate editors, second-year law review members may choose to run for a position on the Law Review's editorial board; the editorial board manages the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial board presently consists of positions such as editor-in-chief, managing editor, executive articles editor, executive comments editor, articles editors, comments editors, research editor, and online editor. The board is the managing body and carries out day-to-day law review operations; third-year non-editorial board members serve as senior editors and advisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online companion content standards and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Penn Statim, the online companion, contains the Law Review's printed content in electronic format, as well as exclusive online scholarship and The Forum Blog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penn Statim accepts exclusive online scholarship submitted by academics, professionals, and law students; The Forum Blog is a less formal platform for short blog posts on contemporary legal issues, indicating different expectations (less formal, shorter pieces) for online content versus print.
